Lenehans Purchasing
V7.47.14 · built 2026-11-27 ·
What’s new ▾
  • 📦 Goods-in check reads photos and scans: drop a picture (JPG/PNG) or a scanned PDF and Claude reads the invoice through the web app (needs Code.gs V7.47.14); when a PDF doesn’t add up, a 🤖 Read it with Claude button does the same — the result says it was read by Claude, so check a few lines · zentrada invoices read (numbers on a line of their own after the position number, description above and below, code from “# LAN332”, barcode from “EAN Code”) and compared with “Value items net” (shipping left out) · supplier names like “ZENTRADA - EU” shown in full
  • 📦 Goods-in check: the “New product? … type its SKU” box starts with the invoice code (most new items are set up under it) · a typed SKU that isn’t the invoice code and isn’t in the dashboard is checked once (“BB-CP31 isn’t the invoice code BB-CP315 … click Use again if it’s right”) — Linnworks skips lines whose SKU doesn’t exist · a typed new SKU still not in Linnworks a day later is flagged on the line
  • 📦 Goods-in check — FIX: Finish and Export always writes the invoice’s quantity in units at the unit price. V7.47.7–V7.47.11 sent lines with a Linnworks pack size as packs (BB-WS203: 1 at €26.88 instead of 12 at €2.24) and Linnworks booked them as 1 — any PO exported with those versions needs its quantities checked
  • 📦 Goods-in check: suppliers are matched on their code (BLA001), so “BLA001- BLACKSPUR” and “BLA001 - Blackspur Ltd” are the same supplier everywhere in the check · when a code isn’t found under the supplier you picked, every supplier’s codes in Linnworks are searched with the same rules (exact, prefix ignored, leading zeros ignored) — used only when it’s one product, and the line says whose code it was (“supplier code “CW104” held under BLA001”)
  • 📦 Goods-in check: the supplier is also worked out from the codes — when most of an invoice’s codes belong to one supplier in Linnworks, that supplier is used (Hamble’s invoice → BLA001 Blackspur, whose codes BD401, AC101… are held under Blackspur), with a note saying so; if you typed another supplier it offers a one-click switch instead · supplier names written “BLA001- BLACKSPUR” (no space before the dash) are now recognised from the invoice text
  • 📦 Goods-in check: the supplier codes held in Linnworks are matched with the same leeway — prefix ignored (BB-AC101 ↔ AC101) and leading zeros ignored (Curust LR0750 ↔ LR750, LR0375D ↔ LR375D) — only when it leads to one product of that supplier; the line says which Linnworks code it used
  • 📦 Goods-in check: code variants — an invoice code with or without a short prefix finds our SKU when it’s the only match (Blackspur BB-AC101 → AC101, CG322 → BB-CG322) · sterling invoices (Hamble/Blackspur): prices are converted to euro at the rate printed on the invoice, so they compare with Linnworks and the PO is exported in euro (£2,460.22 → €2,934.95); a button switches back to £ if a supplier’s costs are kept in sterling · invoice number read from a heading row (“INVOICE No. / ACCOUNT No.” with the values below)
  • 📦 Goods-in check: Ronseal / Sherwin-Williams invoices read (units per case · cases · units · price per unit · price per case · value · VAT): the net value is found from its VAT columns, quantities come out in units at the unit price, the PO from “YOUR ORDER REF”, barcodes from “PRODUCT REFERENCE” · pack sizes in Linnworks: whole packs are exported as packs at the pack price so Linnworks books the right units; part packs are flagged before export (Curust sugar soap: 2 with a pack of 3 would book 6) · the minimum-order warning from V7.47.5 is back in (V7.47.6 was built without it)
  • 📦 Goods-in check: warns when an invoice quantity is below the supplier’s minimum order in Linnworks — the PO import raises it to the minimum, so the PO wouldn’t match the invoice (Curust 047002: 1 invoiced, minimum 2, +€11.50). Shown on the line and as a step before Finish and Export. Needs GoodsInLearn V1.3
  • ⭐ Email designer: a live “26K+ reviews ★★★★★ Trustpilot” line under the banner, from today’s Trustpilot count (a new banner without the printed line goes with it; tick “line under the banner” off for the old banner) · the score above the reviews is now one tidy line: “Excellent ★★★★★ 4.8 out of 5 · based on 26,113 reviews”
  • 🐞 Email check “Past emails”: every product an email sold is now counted — each email used to keep only its 200 best sellers by €, so cheaper lines (HW131, BB-CR200) showed fewer sales or “never featured” · the history rebuilds itself every night (web app Code.gs V7.47.5) and says how fresh it is · “never featured” now reads “no email sales yet” (it counts sales, not whether a product was in an email)
  • 📦 Goods-in check reads far more invoice layouts: when no known layout fits, it finds the code, then the quantity and price that multiply to the line total (with a discount if there is one) — units like “ea (Each)”, prices like “25.95/ea”, the quantity before or after the code, and VAT columns after the total are all fine (Dosco SI00083916: 47 lines, €1,635.25 to the cent). Copy-and-paste from a PDF viewer works too, even when every cell comes out on its own line. Dropping the PDF itself is still the surest way
  • 📦 Goods-in check: the invoice becomes the PO — Finish and Export now lists the steps: ☐ delete the buyer’s PO in Linnworks (the import can’t overwrite it), every line matched, each cost change / new product ticked “updated in Linnworks”, then export at the invoice’s costs (back orders left out). Export is 🔒 until every line has a SKU, and asks twice while ticks are missing. Each cost line shows retail, margin now → at the new cost, and the retail that keeps today’s margin. A new product made in Linnworks today can be linked by typing its SKU. Ticks are shared per invoice (web app Code.gs V7.47.3), so anyone can carry on
  • 📦 Goods-in check: a code you link by hand is now linked for the whole team, not just this computer (needs the web app Code.gs V7.47.2 — it keeps them in a GOODSIN_LINKS tab). Each link says who made it, and ✕ Unlink removes a wrong one for everyone. Links already made on a computer are shared the first time it opens the check
  • 📦 Goods-in check: reads “Ordered · Dispatched · To Follow” invoices (International Tool Industries) — the delivery is what was dispatched, and a line with nothing dispatched shows as ⏳ To follow (on back order), not 🆓 free · codes on their own (“73843 MASONRY…”) no longer read as a quantity · “19-1032-013-” matches 19-1032-013 · a supplier code found at the end of our barcode · an invoice line and a PO line with the same quantity and a code one character apart or a similar name are paired as 🔍 Same product? for you to check · “Nett Price” read as the invoice’s net total

⚙️ Setup required — PO Deliveries sheet

This tab reads from a PO_Deliveries sheet tab in the QueryData spreadsheet, populated by an Apps Script sync. To set it up:

  1. Open the QueryData sheet → Extensions → Apps Script
  2. Add a second sync function (e.g. syncDeliveries()) using the SQL below
  3. Run it once manually to create the PO_Deliveries tab and note its sheet GID
  4. Get the CSV export URL:
    https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LnMn_BU0DIHSOihsTVS0kl0bWITWlxayvdgfMtYoKyQ/export?format=csv&gid=YOUR_GID
  5. Paste the URL above and click Load Deliveries
  6. Optionally set a daily trigger on syncDeliveries() to keep it fresh
▶ Show SQL for Apps Script 
DECLARE @TODAY DATETIME = GETDATE();
DECLARE @PAST  DATETIME = DATEADD(DAY,-90,GETDATE());
SELECT
  p.ExternalInvoiceNumber PONumber, s.SupplierName, CAST(' '+si.ItemNumber AS NVARCHAR(51)) SKU,
  si.ItemTitle, pi.Quantity OrderedQty, pi.Delivered ReceivedQty,
  pi.Quantity-pi.Delivered OutstandingQty,
  CAST(pi.Cost AS DECIMAL(10,2)) UnitCost,
  CAST((pi.Quantity-pi.Delivered)*pi.Cost AS DECIMAL(10,2)) OutstandingValue,
  CONVERT(VARCHAR(10),p.DateOfPurchase,103) PODate,
  CONVERT(VARCHAR(10),p.QuotedDeliveryDate,103) ExpectedDelivery,
  CONVERT(VARCHAR(10),p.DateOfDelivery,103) ActualDelivery,
  p.Status POStatus,
  DATEDIFF(DAY,p.QuotedDeliveryDate,@TODAY) DaysOverdue
FROM Purchase p
JOIN PurchaseItem pi ON pi.fkPurchasId=p.pkPurchaseID
JOIN StockItem si ON si.pkStockItemID=pi.fkStockItemId
JOIN Supplier s ON s.pkSupplierId=p.fkSupplierId
WHERE p.DateOfPurchase>=@PAST AND pi.Quantity>0 AND p.Status NOT IN('CANCELLED')
ORDER BY CASE p.Status WHEN 'PENDING' THEN 1 WHEN 'PLACED' THEN 2 WHEN 'PARTIAL' THEN 3 WHEN 'DELIVERED' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END, p.QuotedDeliveryDate ASC

💶 Price Review — price-point increases

Applies your rules to every SKU's list price (inc-VAT), counts what changes, and costs the margin effect using the last 12 months' sales. Volumes assumed unchanged — see the sensitivity line.

Rules
Only SKUs with a list price in Linnworks are analysed. Margin = (price ÷ 1.23) − cost.
Run the analysis to see how many SKUs change and the margin effect.

🏷️ EAN-13 Barcode Generator

Turns each SKU into a valid internal EAN-13 (prefix 20 — the range reserved for in-store use, so it never clashes with real product barcodes at the till). Each SKU gets a permanent number from a register, so the same SKU always produces the same barcode. Enter SKUs (or bin codes), one per line.

The register is saved in this browser. Export register (CSV) · Reset
